title: Acquired aplastic anemia
subtitle: Immune destruction of hematopoietic stem cells · pancytopenia + empty marrow · grade severity, exclude hypoplastic MDS and inherited BMF, HLA-type early; MSD HCT if young, otherwise hATG + cyclosporine + eltrombopag
source: Compiled from ASH 2026, BSH 2024 and ASTCT 2024 guidelines · NIH / EBMT data · FDA labels · primary trial reports verified against PubMed, October 2026.

blocks.heading: Definition & severity
rows: Pancytopenia + hypocellular marrow with no abnormal infiltrate, no fibrosis and no MDS-defining dysplasia/cytogenetics. A diagnosis of exclusion
Cellularity <25% (or 25–50% with <30% residual hematopoietic cells) + ≥2 of: ANC <0.5 · plt <20 · retic <60 ×109/L
SAA criteria + ANC <0.2 — highest infection mortality; treat urgently
Hypocellular marrow + cytopenias not meeting SAA. Split by transfusion dependence
blocks.footnote: Severity, age and donor availability drive every treatment decision.

blocks.heading: Causes
rows: Most cases. Cytotoxic T cells (IFN-γ, TNF) destroy HSPCs; responds to IST
Chloramphenicol, gold, carbamazepine, felbamate, sulfonamides; benzene. Chemo/radiation aplasia is expected, not AA
AA weeks–months after a seronegative (non-A–E) hepatitis, often young men; immune, treat as AA
Pregnancy · PNH · LGL leukemia · thymoma · SLE · eosinophilic fasciitis · viruses (EBV, HIV); parvovirus B19 = red cells only
Short stature, radial/thumb anomalies, café-au-lait. Chromosome breakage (DEB/MMC). Do not give standard Cy conditioning
Nail dystrophy, leukoplakia, early graying, pulmonary fibrosis, cirrhosis. Telomere length flow-FISH; TERT/TERC. Poor IST response
Monocytopenia, B/NK lymphopenia, MAC/HPV infections, lymphedema; hypocellular MDS risk
SDS: neutropenia + pancreatic insufficiency (SBDS). DBA: red-cell aplasia, macrocytosis, high eADA
blocks.footnote: Suspect inherited BMF in the young, with family history, physical stigmata or IST failure — and screen a sibling donor for the same disorder.

blocks.heading: Treatment pathway — severe / very severe AA

boxes: MSD bone marrow HCT up front
Marrow graft (PBSC worse: more cGVHD, lower OS)
Cy + ATG conditioning; add fludarabine if older
ASH 2026 / BSH: HCT over IST to age 40;
ASTCT: no fixed cutoff for fit older adults

chains.header: No MSD, age >40, or not fit for HCT
boxes: 1. hATG + cyclosporine + eltrombopag
hATG 40 mg/kg/d ×4 + CsA from day 1
+ eltrombopag 150 mg/d ×6 mo (RACE, NIH)
rATG inferior up front (Scheinberg 2011)
2. Reassess counts at 3 and 6 months
responses are slow — do not judge before 3 mo
responder: CsA continued, then slow taper
Up-front MUD HCT instead
young + severe infection + MUD readily available
(BSH); age <40: MUD or IST both acceptable (ASH)

chains.header: Refractory (no response by 3–6 mo) or relapse
boxes: Second line by 6 mo after ATG
<40 y: HCT (MUD or haplo-PTCy) over 2nd ATG
40–60 y: HCT favored · >60 y: HCT or 2nd ATG
relapse: CsA ± EPAG; HCT or 2nd ATG (>60: 2nd ATG)
no HCT: eltrombopag alone (44%, Olnes 2012)
By transfusion need
not transfusion-dependent: observe, CBC q1–3 mo
transfusion-dependent or worsening: CsA ±
eltrombopag, or treat as SAA (hATG-based IST)

blocks.heading: Pearls
items: HLA-type siblings in week 1 — donor availability is the first branch point
Hypocellular marrow in the elderly is normal; read cellularity for age
Never start ATG during active uncontrolled infection if avoidable; treat infection first
Short telomeres or a germline variant change management: IST works poorly, Fanconi needs reduced-intensity conditioning

blocks.heading: Workup
items: CBC + diff, retic, smear — macrocytosis common; no blasts, no dysplasia. HbF (raised in inherited BMF)
Exclude mimics: B12, folate, copper; LFTs; HBV, HCV, HIV, EBV, CMV, parvovirus B19 PCR; ANA/dsDNA; T-cell flow / TCR clonality (LGL); CT chest if thymoma suspected
High-sensitivity PNH flow (granulocyte FLAER, 0.01%) at diagnosis
Marrow aspirate + trephine: cellularity, dysplasia, blasts, reticulin; karyotype (± FISH 5/7) + myeloid NGS panel
Inherited screen: DEB/MMC breakage, telomere length flow-FISH, germline panel when suspected
HLA-type patient + full siblings at diagnosis; start an unrelated-donor search early. Ferritin, creatinine, CMV serostatus, pregnancy test

blocks.heading: Clones · AA vs hypoplastic MDS
rows: Clones grow over time; worse outcome, higher MDS/AML risk
Favor hypoplastic MDS → HCT; −7 after IST = high-risk evolution
Myeloid-gene mutations in ~1/3, CH in 47%, low VAF — not MDS by itself
Hypo-MDS: dysplastic megakaryocytes, blasts, CD34+ ↑, fibrosis. AA: fatty marrow, lymphoid aggregates, mild dyserythropoiesis only

blocks.heading: Supportive care
items: Products leukoreduced; irradiated around ATG and for HCT candidates. No family-donor transfusions before HCT — sensitizes to donor antigens, raises graft rejection
Prophylactic platelets at <10 (higher if febrile/bleeding); restrictive RBC thresholds
ANC <0.5: mold-active azole + antibacterial prophylaxis ASH 2026; HSV/VZV prophylaxis with ATG. Azoles raise CsA levels
No routine G-CSF — no survival benefit (Tichelli 2011); short-term use only in severe infection
Iron overload: chelate (deferasirox or deferoxamine); avoid deferiprone (agranulocytosis). Phlebotomy after recovery

blocks.heading: Response & timing — NIH criteria
rows: No longer meets SAA criteria; usually transfusion-independent
blocks.footnote: Assess at 3 and 6 months. Median time to first response 3.0 mo with eltrombopag vs 8.8 mo without (RACE). Start second-line therapy no later than 6 mo after ATG (ASH 2026).

blocks.heading: Relapse & clonal evolution
items: Relapse 39% at 4 yr in responders on CsA maintenance — clustered after the 6-mo CsA cut / eltrombopag stop and after CsA stops at 2 yr; ~2/3 respond to CsA ± eltrombopag again Patel Blood 2022, n=178
Clonal evolution 15% at 4 yr; high-risk (myeloid neoplasm or chr 7) 5.7%, with worse OS — not higher than IST alone, but earlier
New cytopenia or falling counts → repeat marrow + karyotype; −7 or MDS/AML → HCT

PNH clones: small clones are common in AA and predict IST response; they can expand after IST into hemolytic PNH — re-check flow at least yearly; complement inhibition only for clinically significant hemolysis

blocks.heading: Agents — dosing
rows: 40 mg/kg/d IV ×4 days over ~4 h (NIH; label: 10–20 mg/kg/d ×8–14 d). Premed acetaminophen + antihistamine; prednisone 1 mg/kg/d ×10 d, taper over 7–14 d
Infusion reactions; serum sickness (fever, rash, arthralgia) ~day 7–14. Platelets before each dose; inpatient
Second IST course or HCT conditioning
3 mg/kg PO q12h (6 mg/kg/d) from day 1 → trough 200–400 µg/L. Responders: continue, then taper slowly (NIH: 2 mg/kg/d to 24 mo)
Nephrotoxicity, HTN, Mg wasting, gingival hyperplasia, PRES. Azole interactions

First-line: 150 mg daily ×6 mo with IST (≥12 y; label ≥2 y, weight/age-based); 75 mg if East/Southeast Asian ancestry or hepatic impairment. Refractory: 50 mg → max 150 mg; stop if no response by 16 wk
Take ≥2 h before or 4 h after cations (antacids, calcium, iron, dairy). LFTs; cataract exam; −7 in 4 (D1–M6 cohort), 7/153 across cohorts. FDA: refractory 2014, first-line 2018
Japan-approved (refractory AA 2019, all AA 2023); not FDA-approved for AA

blocks.heading: Allogeneic HCT
items: MSD vs URD (EBMT, n=1448): URD survival not significantly worse in multivariate analysis, but more acute (25% vs 13%) and chronic GVHD (26% vs 14%). Worst predictor: PBSC graft; also ≥180 d from diagnosis, age ≥20, no ATG Bacigalupo 2015
Marrow over PBSC: age <20 MSD, 5-yr OS 85% vs 73% Schrezenmeier Blood 2007
Haplo with PTCy up front (Hopkins phase 2, n=27): 3-yr OS 92%; aGVHD II–IV 7%, cGVHD 4%; with 400 cGy TBI 20/20 alive DeZern Blood 2023
Guidelines differ: ASTCT 2024 favors MUD/haplo over IST when no MSD; ASH 2026 still favors IST over haplo up front at any age. Conditioning: rATG, fludarabine for MUD/haplo

blocks.heading: Key trials
rows: Randomized, n=120: 6-mo response 68% vs 37%; 3-yr OS 96% vs 76%. Horse ATG is standard
Phase 1–2, n=92: eltrombopag day 1–6 mo cohort CR 58%, ORR 94% vs historical CR 10%, ORR 66%
Phase 3, n=197, hATG + CsA ± EPAG: CR at 3 mo 22% vs 10% (OR 3.2); ORR 6 mo 68% vs 41%; no extra toxicity
Single-arm, n=25: 44% response at 12 wk, multilineage
Randomized, n=192: fewer infections, no OS/EFS benefit — no routine G-CSF
Up-front haplo-PTCy, n=27: 3-yr OS 92%, minimal GVHD

blocks.heading: Pregnancy
items: AA can present or relapse in pregnancy; after IST, 19% of 36 pregnancies relapsed, 34 live births Tichelli 2002
Supportive care (transfusion) is the mainstay; CsA can be continued; avoid ATG and eltrombopag
Low platelets and a PNH clone predict complications — consider LMWH if a PNH clone is present
